document_metadata.purpose: Provide a detailed, testable specification for implementing PHOBOSIA mission Days 6, 7, 8, and 9. This file must be used as the source of mission requirements by a separate coding-agent master prompt.
prerequisites: Phase 2 is complete and implements Days 1 to 5.

The existing mission-state system, daily briefing flow, objective validation, interaction framework, module transitions, screen-rendering framework, and Habitat rest/sleep progression must be reused wherever possible.
The existing PHOBOSIA_Days_1-5_Specification.json must be inspected before modifying shared systems.
document_metadata.source_of_truth: This specification defines the intended Phase 3 gameplay. The actual repository defines the real file paths, identifiers, object names, screen dimensions, transforms, interfaces, and established implementation patterns. Preserve existing working systems and adapt implementation to the actual repository without silently renaming existing objects.

technology_stack: Existing project-specific rendering and interaction utilities

migration_policy.rule: Extend the existing architecture. Do not migrate to another framework or replace working systems simply to implement Phase 3.

requirements: Keep the experience suitable for a modest laptop GPU.
Reuse existing Three.js geometries, materials, textures, cameras, and rendering utilities where appropriate.
Avoid unnecessary high-resolution textures and duplicate assets.
Avoid expensive post-processing and excessive animated effects.
Do not add a physics engine solely for these missions.
Dispose of temporary resources created by new interactions.
Prevent event-listener, texture, and render-loop leaks.

player_experience.outdoor_helmet_hud: Reuse the Phase 2 helmet/visor HUD. Show it outdoors only, except where the established UI intentionally displays a compatible contextual notification.
player_experience.drone_view: First-person remote FPV camera, separate from astronaut movement.
player_experience.movement: Reuse the existing Phase 1 first-person movement system.

scope_exclusions: Do not implement Days 10, 11, 12, 13, or 14 in Phase 3.
Do not implement rover driving or rover terrain-following in this phase.
Do not add new habitat modules or additional buildings.
Do not implement third-person astronaut control.
Do not require a visible drone mesh for Day 9.
Do not introduce a new inventory, crafting, survival, or complex sample-collection system.
Do not present simulated observations as actual NASA discoveries.
Do not claim live NASA telemetry, live drone telemetry, or real instrument readings unless such integrations already exist and have been verified.

mandatory_before_implementation: Read this Phase 3 specification and the actual Phase 2 JSON specification from the repository.
Inspect the existing mission type definitions and mission-state implementation.
Inspect the current daily briefing, objective checklist, objective validation, completion summary, and rest/sleep progression.
Inspect the existing module transition implementation, including fade, loading screen, destination video, skip behaviour, and spawn restoration.
Inspect the existing screen-plane rendering system and how it determines which screens are active.
Inspect the existing terrain generator, selected Mars region, coordinate bounds, terrain scale, and any available height data.
Inspect the existing Day 5 route-plan data and how it is saved.
Inspect the existing Drone_Object reference, Mission Control screens, controls, camera architecture, and input handling.
Inspect existing screen plane dimensions, aspect ratios, transforms, orientations, parent objects, and material assignments.
Inspect actual asset filenames before referencing any images, videos, textures, or models.
Run the existing build and tests before changes and record baseline failures.

identifier_policy: Do not rename existing scene objects, triggers, screen planes, exported TypeScript symbols, or established state keys merely for naming consistency.
Do not invent screen-plane names before inspecting the actual scene.
Do not move existing objects to make an interaction easier without explicit necessity and documented approval.
If a required target or control does not exist, report the gap and reuse the nearest appropriate existing interaction pattern.
New identifiers may be introduced for mission records and objective IDs when necessary, provided they do not conflict with existing names.

standard_daily_loop: Show the briefing for the active mission day.
Update objective progress from actual mission state.
Save required records when the player confirms an observation or analysis.
Show a completion summary when the day is complete.
Require the established Habitat rest/sleep interaction to advance to the next day.
progression_rules: Only the current campaign day may be active.
A day must not complete merely because a UI panel was opened.
Required records must be validated before their objectives are marked complete.
Incomplete required objectives must block rest/sleep progression.
Repeated confirmation must not create duplicate records or repeat completion side effects.
State changes must be idempotent where appropriate.
Leaving and re-entering a module must not erase saved observations.
Day 9 completion may prepare the existing Day 10 state, but must not implement Day 10 gameplay.

shared_state.instruction: Extend the existing mission-state types and persistence mechanism rather than creating a competing state system.

potential_fields_if_missing.routePlan: Existing Day 5 route-plan record, reused if available

record_rules: Do not store Three.js Object3D instances, DOM nodes, callbacks, or camera objects in mission records.
Each record must have a stable identifier.
Store source record IDs when one record is derived from another.
Clearly label generated values and interpretations as simulated.
Use the existing persistence strategy and avoid adding a backend.

visual_identity.style: Professional, distinctive PHOBOSIA mission interface inspired by aerospace and scientific observation consoles.
principles: Distinct visual states for available, active, complete, and unavailable interactions
avoid: UI that obscures the main outdoor view

3d_screen_rendering: Inspect each real screen plane's width, height, aspect ratio, orientation, and transform before designing its content.
Fit each interface to the corresponding screen geometry.
Use a flat CanvasTexture or the existing screen-rendering mechanism where appropriate.
Do not project flat interface text onto spherical geometry unless the actual display surface is spherical.
Correct stretching, mirroring, clipping, upside-down text, incorrect orientation, and curved text distortion.
Use appropriate texture resolution without excessive VRAM use.
Do not recreate textures every frame unless the existing rendering architecture requires it.
Dispose of textures created specifically for a screen when that screen is permanently removed.
Activate only the relevant screens for the current module and interaction.
Do not illuminate or populate every screen in every module at once.
If a physical screen is too small for detailed controls, show a concise summary and use the established interaction UI for detailed input.
input_and_interaction: Reuse the established E-key interaction convention.
Show contextual interaction prompts only when the player is in range and the interaction is available.
Prevent a single key press from activating multiple conflicting interactions.
When a console is open, prevent gameplay movement keys from unintentionally moving the astronaut.
Provide visible success, unavailable, incomplete, and recoverable-error feedback.
Clean up listeners when a UI, mode, or scene is closed.
Preserve the existing camera and control state when switching between modules or modes.

requirements: Reuse the existing Phase 2 helmet HUD.
Use actual mission state for statuses.
Do not introduce arbitrary random errors.
Any scripted alert must correspond to an actual mission event or be explicitly identified as scripted simulation.

days.title: Geological Site Survey
days.narrative_purpose: Use the existing Day 5 route-planning work to conduct an initial outdoor geological observation. The astronaut reaches a designated survey area, inspects visible terrain characteristics, and saves a preliminary geological record for later scientific comparison.

briefing.delivery: Use the existing daily briefing system.
required_content: Reminder to use the existing Airlock transition when exiting the habitat
briefing.narrative_guidance: Mission Control has prepared an initial survey target using the existing mission configuration and the Day 5 route plan where available. The astronaut must inspect the surface and record preliminary observations.
briefing.data_truthfulness: Do not present simulated observations as new NASA discoveries or as verified geological conclusions about Mars.

prerequisites.condition: Use the existing Day 5 route-plan record if it is available.
prerequisites.fallback: Use the configured existing survey target if the route-plan record is unavailable. Do not fabricate a saved route plan.

objectives.label: Review the geological survey target
objectives.completion_condition: The player opens the relevant existing Mission Control information and reviews the configured Day 6 target.
objectives.validation: Track the target review in shared mission state. Opening a generic menu does not satisfy this objective.

objectives.label: Reach the designated survey area
objectives.completion_condition: The player enters the valid configured survey area on the existing Mars master terrain.
objectives.validation: Use an existing target marker if one exists. Otherwise configure the target through the existing mission configuration pattern. Do not move unrelated scene objects or change the selected terrain coordinates.

objectives.label: Inspect the surface characteristics
objectives.completion_condition: The player activates the supported geological observation interaction while within the valid target area.
objectives.validation: Reject the interaction when the player is outside the configured valid area.

objectives.label: Save the preliminary geological record
objectives.completion_condition: A valid GeologicalSurveyRecord is saved to shared mission state.
objectives.validation: The record must contain the required fields and must not be created as a result of merely opening the interface.

interactions.result: Display the configured survey target, available Day 5 route-plan summary, and a concise objective checklist.
Run a short, lightweight observation interaction and show a readable observation interface.
Validate the observation selections, save the record, update objective progress, and show a confirmation.

observation_interface.title: GEOLOGICAL FIELD OBSERVATION
observation_interface.presentation: A focused PHOBOSIA-style panel. Keep the outdoor view visible where possible and avoid a long full-screen interruption.
interaction_rules: Use a bounded list of choices rather than a complex scientific instrument simulation.
Do not claim exact mineral composition from terrain geometry alone.
Do not claim actual scientific certainty.
Keep the form usable with keyboard input.
Preserve the player's selections if saving temporarily fails.

optional_fields.routePlanReference: Existing Day 5 route-plan ID or null
optional_fields.missionTimestamp: Use the existing mission-time convention if available

rules: Use the project's existing record naming and typing conventions where possible.
Use a stable identifier so later phases can reference this record.
Repeated saves should update or reopen the existing Day 6 record rather than create duplicate records.
Never store Three.js scene objects in this record.

screen_requirements.activation: Only when the relevant Mission Control screen is active.

content: Contextual scan prompt when in range

screen_requirements.activation: Only during the geological observation interaction.

failure_recovery: If the target is missing, report the missing configuration clearly and do not mark the objective complete.
If the player is outside the valid survey area, display a contextual instruction.
If saving fails, keep the objective incomplete and allow retry.
If a record already exists, allow the player to review it without duplicating it.
acceptance_tests: Day 6 briefing appears only when Day 6 is active.
The existing Day 5 route-plan record is reused when available.
The survey target is consistent with the existing master terrain and configured coordinates.
The scan interaction is unavailable outside its valid area.
A valid GeologicalSurveyRecord is saved with all required fields.
Day 6 cannot complete without the saved record.
Repeated save attempts do not create duplicate records.
The outdoor HUD does not cover indoor or full-screen interfaces.

days.title: Science Lab Analysis
days.narrative_purpose: Analyse the saved Day 7 surface observation in the existing Science Lab. Where available, compare it with the Day 6 geological survey, choose a cautious interpretation, and save a scientific analysis record for later mission synthesis.

required_content: Reference to the saved Day 7 observation
Instruction to review the source record
Instruction to compare earlier observations when available
Instruction to select and save an interpretation
briefing.narrative_guidance: The Science Lab has received the surface observation from Day 7. The astronaut must inspect the source record, compare relevant notes, select a cautious interpretation, and save the result.
briefing.data_truthfulness: This is a simulated educational interpretation, not a claim of actual mineral identification or a new scientific discovery.

prerequisites.failure_message: No saved Day 7 surface observation is available. Complete the surface observation before analysing it.
prerequisites.recovery: Do not fabricate a source record. Keep the analysis objective unavailable until the required record exists.

prerequisites.condition: Use the Day 6 GeologicalSurveyRecord for comparison if available.
prerequisites.fallback: Display a clear unavailable state and allow analysis to continue when the mission rules permit.

days.title: Drone Survey
days.narrative_purpose: Conduct a remote survey of the existing Mars master terrain from Mission Control using a first-person drone FPV view. The player inspects a designated area, captures a simulated survey record, exits FPV, and returns to the astronaut's normal camera and controls.

briefing.delivery: Use the existing daily briefing system.
required_content: Explanation that the survey is remotely operated from Mission Control
Instructions for entering and exiting drone FPV mode
briefing.narrative_guidance: Mission Control authorises a short remote terrain survey. The astronaut will enter a first-person drone view, inspect the configured area, save a survey record, and return to Mission Control.
briefing.data_truthfulness: Drone telemetry and observations are simulated unless an actual verified data integration exists.

operating_model.reference_object_instruction: Inspect the actual object type, transform, hierarchy, and existing use before implementation. Do not assume it is a visible mesh.
movement_requirements: Use a dedicated drone-control state separate from astronaut movement.
Provide clear control hints while FPV is active.
Prevent drone controls from triggering astronaut movement.
Constrain the drone to the configured survey bounds.
Use existing terrain-height or collision queries if they are already available.
If terrain queries are unavailable, use a lightweight configurable altitude and boundary constraint.
Do not rewrite the terrain system.
Do not add a full flight-physics system or a new physics engine.
camera_requirements: Reuse the existing render loop and camera architecture where possible.
Enter FPV only after an explicit action at the relevant Mission Control interaction.
Store the astronaut camera/control state before switching modes.
Disable astronaut movement while FPV is active.
Display a clear DRONE FPV — REMOTE CONTROL indicator.
Restore the previous astronaut camera and controls on exit.
Use one cleanup path for normal exit and unexpected interruption.
Do not create a second uncontrolled animation loop.
Do not allow repeated activation to create multiple active drone cameras or duplicate listeners.
operating_model.helmet_hud_policy: Do not display the astronaut's outdoor helmet HUD while the drone FPV view is active. Use a separate minimal drone status overlay.

objectives.label: Return to Mission Control
objectives.completion_condition: The player exits FPV and the astronaut camera, controls, and input state are restored.
